Role: Senior Product Designer
Company: SimpleStudy
Location: Remote, Europe (preferably Western / continental); relocation to Lisbon possible
Job Type: Full-time

About SimpleStudy
SimpleStudy is an AI exam prep platform that students find and choose for themselves.
In some numbers:
• 
1.5M+ students across the UK, Ireland, Brazil, South Africa, and Australia
• 
40–50k new students every week
• 
Web, mobile, and desktop apps
• 
$4M seed round with investors from Strava, OpenAI, and Meta
The traction came fast. Now the company is refounding: rebuilding the brand, the design language, and the product experience from scratch. The product grew like a Jenga tower, one feature on top of another. The job now is to rebuild it as a pyramid.
The team is ~30 people, remote with a Lisbon office — lean, product-led, and deliberately not a typical edtech company.
You'll report to José, the Founding Designer, and work with him as a partner. José tends to lead early framing and direction. You bring strong craft and take the work to the finish line, in close sync with engineering. You both shape the new design language, and you push back with a better idea when you see one.

What you are expected to do:
• 
Shape the new design language and brand: design system, rebrand, and the new mobile app.
• 
Own the full design process — from an ambiguous problem to a polished, shipped solution.
• 
Drive the consumer experience: onboarding, social features, retention, and the learning loop.
• 
Work in close sync with engineers and PM, not as a handoff step - polish the implementation together until it feels right.
• 
Bring your own initiatives and say "no, but…" when you see a better way.
• 
Raise the bar for the whole design team.

What you need to succeed:
• 
High craft — your visual work is polished and intentional; the details reveal your thinking.
• 
Storytelling over process — you take an ambiguous problem, frame it, and make it simple. Your portfolio shows artifacts, not diagrams; it has a point of view.
• 
Consumer instinct — you've shipped B2C products that people chose to use. You understand product metrics and use them as input, but you lead with feel and craft.
• 
Opinions with backbone — you have a design philosophy, can defend it under pushback, and bring your own initiatives. You don't wait to be told what to build.
• 
Energy and curiosity — you're an interesting person with a life outside work, and you leave people energised after a conversation.
• 
English — fluent, written and spoken.

What would be a plus:
• 
A standout specialty: prototyping, illustration, animation, or motion.
• 
Experience with social or viral product mechanics.
• 
Background at consumer companies like Spotify or Strava.
• 
Early-stage or founding designer experience.
• 
Comfortable in code: prototyping or polishing the front end.

What you get:
• 
Build from scratch, at scale — a new design language for a product already used by 1.5M+ students.
• 
A strong partner - work closely with José, the Founding Designer (ex-Shopify), with direct access to the founders.
• 
Equity — generous stock options, early enough for them to matter.
• 
Remote Europe — work from where you choose, with in-person meetups three times a year; relocation support if you want to move to Lisbon.
• 
Competitive salary — no fixed budget, flexible.

How to apply:
A deck or a walkthrough video is fine. Show the work, keep it curated.
Please email links to your LinkedIn / Resume and portfolio to 

The vacancy is proudly presented by the hirehire recruiting agency.
"Craft matters here from day one. You'll rebuild the brand, the design system and the product together with José, a founding designer who cares a lot about how things feel. 1.5M students, real traction, and a team that picks quality over speed."
— Tanya Sivo
Product Design Expert, hirehire

6e5450e99c4ca8c8.description: 12 of the top 15 pharma generic companies in the world trust Leucine to manufacture the drugs that reach millions of patients every day. Pharma manufacturing is one of the last large industries still running on paper, Excel, and tribal knowledge. A single missed step in a batch record can mean a recall, a regulatory warning, or a drug that should never have left the plant. Leucine is the AI platform replacing all of it. Series A, backed by top-tier global investors, 60+ pharma enterprises in production, and the team that's going to define this category. ### About the Role We build software for pharmaceutical quality teams — the systems that decide whether a batch ships, whether an auditor walks away satisfied, and whether a deviation gets closed properly. That means every feature we release has to be correct, documented, and defensible to a regulator. Shipping fast and shipping validated are both non-negotiable, and that tension is exactly where this role lives. You'll work alongside our Associate Product Manager as the operational backbone of the product function: testing what engineering builds, writing the test cases that define "done," producing the validation and CSV documentation our customers depend on, and keeping the paper trail clean while the product moves quickly. This is not a role where you'll be told what to think about the roadmap on day one. It *is* a role where you'll see every feature up close, learn a regulated domain most PMs never touch, and build the judgment that makes a strong PM two years from now. If you want to learn product by being in the details of how it actually gets shipped, this is that seat. ### What You'll Do ### Test what we build - Run structured functional test passes on new features before they reach customers — happy paths, edge cases, permissions, and the ugly states nobody designed for - File bugs that engineers can act on immediately: clear repro steps, expected vs. actual, environment, severity - Verify fixes and run regression sweeps ahead of each release so old bugs stay dead - Coordinate and support UAT with internal stakeholders and, occasionally, customers ### Write the test cases - Translate PRDs and user stories into test cases with explicit preconditions, steps, and expected results - Maintain and version the test case library as modules evolve — so the suite reflects the product as it is, not as it was two quarters ago - Flag gaps in requirements early: if a spec can't be turned into a test case, it isn't finished, and you'll be the one to say so ### Own the CSV and validation documentation - Draft and maintain Computer System Validation deliverables — user and functional requirement specs, traceability matrices, IQ/OQ/PQ protocols, and test scripts - Execute validation protocols and capture objective evidence (screenshots, logs, timestamps) to a standard that survives audit scrutiny - Compile executed validation packages, log and route deviations, and keep documentation aligned with 21 CFR Part 11, GxP, and ALCOA+ expectations - Work with engineering to keep validation artifacts in sync with what actually shipped ### Write the documents that surround the product - Release notes, user guides, in-app help content, and configuration guides - Internal enablement material so sales, CS, and implementation teams can speak to new functionality accurately - Meeting notes that become action items with owners, not notes that die in a doc ### Support the APM on everything else - Backlog hygiene — grooming tickets, chasing missing detail, keeping the board honest - Competitor teardowns, feature research, and quick customer-facing artifacts - Demo environment setup and test data preparation - Pulling the data needed to answer "did this actually work?" **Requirements** ### What We're Looking For (Must-Haves) - 0–2 years of experience — new graduates welcome. What matters is evidence you can be trusted with detail - Exceptional written clarity. Most of your output is documents other people act on; ambiguity in your writing becomes rework for someone else - Genuine rigor and patience for detail. In this domain, an untested edge case or an undocumented step is a real problem, not a nitpick - Comfort using software deeply — you can learn a complex product quickly and reason about how it *should* behave, not just how it does - High agency. You'll often be the person who notices the gap first, and we expect you to raise it rather than route around it - Bachelor's degree in engineering, life sciences, pharmacy, computer science, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience) ### Good to Have - Exposure to pharma, biotech, medical devices, or any regulated environment — QA, QC, regulatory affairs, or validation experience is a strong plus - Familiarity with GxP, 21 CFR Part 11, GAMP 5, or CSV/CSA concepts - Hands-on QA or test-case-writing experience, manual or automated - Comfort with tools like JIRA/Linear, Notion/Confluence, Figma, Postman, or Playwright - Familiarity with AI-assisted tools (Claude, Cursor, and similar) to move faster on documentation and testing - Basic SQL or spreadsheet fluency for answering simple product questions **Benefits** - Be part of a fast-growing SaaS company transforming the future of pharmaceutical manufacturing through cutting-edge technology - Collaborate with a passionate, high-performing team building innovative AI-powered digital solutions - Take ownership of impactful client implementations from day one, with ample opportunities for learning, career growth, and professional development - Enjoy a competitive compensation package designed to reward your contributions - Comprehensive Health Insurance with industry-leading coverage for your peace of mind - Complimentary Meals & Refreshments: Stay energized with unlimited breakfast, lunch, snacks, and dinner provided at the office - Family-Friendly Leave Policies, including Paternity Leave and Compassionate Leave, to support you through life's important moments

6e45fcccb0172f93.description: Strategic Partnerships Associate — Teler About FreJun FreJun builds voice and telephony products. FreJun Dialer is business calling integrated with CRMs and ATSs, used by sales, support, and recruitment teams. Teler is our programmable voice and telephony layer for developers and AI teams. It provides APIs for call control, media streaming, number provisioning, and call handling, allowing teams to put real phone calls behind AI voice agents. Teler is where this role sits. --- About the Role We are looking for a Strategic Partnerships Associate to help get Teler embedded inside products built by other companies — including AI agent platforms, voice and automation tools, CRMs, and IT services firms/system integrators. This is a technical partnerships role. You will: - Map the AI voice, agent, automation, CRM, and IT-services ecosystem. - Identify and qualify technically relevant partners. - Run developer- and CTO-level conversations. - Demonstrate how Teler works. - Build small reference integrations and sample applications. - Help partners integrate Teler into their products. - Take partners from first conversation → first test call → first production call. - Work with Sales, Product, Engineering, and Marketing on partner opportunities. - Turn partner feedback into actionable product improvements. What You'll Actually Do 1. Find and qualify the right partners Research companies building: - AI voice agents - AI agent platforms - Voice/LLM tooling - Automation platforms - CRMs and ATSs - Contact-center software - Developer platforms - IT services and system integrations You'll read their documentation, understand their existing architecture and voice stack, and determine exactly where Teler could fit. This isn't about collecting logos. You'll need to answer: Why this partner? Why Teler? Why now? --- 2. Have conversations developers actually care about You'll own first-touch outreach through: - Email - LinkedIn - GitHub - Developer communities - Discord/Slack communities - Events Your outreach should demonstrate that you actually understand what the company is building. You'll run discovery calls and uncover: - What are they building? - What does their current voice infrastructure look like? - What isn't working? - Who owns the technical decision? - How difficult would integration be? - What volume could they generate? - What would it take to reach production? --- 3. Build and integrate This is why the coding requirement exists. You should be able to work directly with a partner's engineering team without needing a FreJun engineer on every call. You'll: - Build reference integrations. - Create sample applications. - Write API examples and code snippets. - Create Postman collections. - Walk developers through Teler's APIs. - Help partners configure accounts and credentials. - Assist with number provisioning. - Drive the first successful test call. - Help reach the first production call. - Read logs and reproduce integration issues. - Determine whether an issue is in the partner's code, Teler, or the network. - Give Engineering a clean, reproducible technical report when escalation is required. --- Technical Skills We Expect You should be comfortable with: APIs - REST APIs - Authentication - Headers - Request/response structures - HTTP status codes - Rate limits - Pagination - Idempotency - Error handling Webhooks - Event-driven architecture - Signature verification - Retries - Ordering - Idempotent handlers - Debugging missed events Coding You should be able to write working code in at least one of: Python / JavaScript / TypeScript / Go / Java / PHP You don't need to be a senior engineer. You do need to be able to build a working integration without hand-holding. Developer Tools You should be comfortable with: - Postman - curl - Browser DevTools - Logs - Basic observability/debugging Voice & AI You should either already understand, or be able to quickly learn: - SIP - DIDs and number provisioning - Inbound vs outbound calls - Call control - Media/audio streaming - Codecs at a conceptual level - Latency and jitter - STT → LLM → TTS architecture - Streaming vs turn-based interaction - Barge-in/interruption handling - Function/tool calling - Where the telephony layer fits underneath an AI voice agent Prior telephony experience is not mandatory. Engineering judgement is. --- What We're Looking For You may be a strong fit if you've spent the last 1–2+ years doing something like: - Software engineering - Full-stack/backend/frontend development - Building and shipping your own startup/product - Solutions engineering - Integration engineering - Implementation engineering - Developer relations with substantial coding - Technical support engineering involving real development - Hands-on technical product work - Building substantial open-source projects We need evidence. Be prepared to show: - GitHub/GitLab - Portfolio - Live product - Public project - Or another concrete example of software you built During the interview, you'll walk us through something you've built: What problem did it solve? What did you build? Why did you make those technical choices? What broke? What would you change? --- What Does NOT Count This role is not intended for candidates whose technical experience is limited to: - Sales - SDR/BD - Account management - Partnerships - Recruitment - Marketing - Agency work - Consulting without software ownership - Coursework - Bootcamp certificates - Tutorial projects - Being "comfortable with technology" We mean you have actually built and shipped software. --- The Other Skills That Matter Strong writing You'll write a lot: - Partner outreach - Technical briefs - Integration guides - Internal notes - Follow-ups - Documentation We value precise, direct writing over corporate jargon. Commercial judgement Partnerships aren't about collecting logos. You should be able to determine: Is this partner actually worth the integration effort? Ownership There isn't an established partnership playbook waiting for you. You'll often be the first person trying something. We expect you to: figure it out → run it → measure it → document it → improve it. Organization You'll likely have multiple partners at different stages simultaneously. Keeping track of: - Next steps - Technical blockers - Integration status - Opportunities - Follow-ups - CRM data is part of the job. --- How We'll Measure Success Your success will primarily be measured by: Partner Activation Partners reaching their first production call. Partner Pipeline Partner-sourced and partner-influenced opportunities and revenue. Velocity Time from first conversation → test call → production. Technical Self-Sufficiency How many partner technical conversations you can handle without Engineering. Enablement Integrations, documentation, demos, and technical assets shipped. Coverage Quality technical conversations with relevant partners. Product Feedback Whether partner feedback is specific and actionable enough to improve Teler. --- Nice to Have Any of these will help: - CPaaS experience - SIP/VoIP - Contact-center software - IVR - AI voice tooling - LLM APIs - STT/TTS - AI agent frameworks - IT services / system integrator experience - Developer relations - Open-source contributions - CRM/outreach tooling - Automation or scripting - Technical blogging/documentation --- Why Join? You'll be working on a category that is still being built. Teler provides programmable voice infrastructure for teams building AI voice applications, with FreJun's own telephony infrastructure and regulatory setup. You'll get: - Direct exposure to founders and department leads. - Fast decision-making. - The opportunity to build the partnerships function from the ground up. - Hands-on exposure to AI voice, APIs, telephony, and developer ecosystems. - A role that can develop into Partnerships, Solutions Engineering, Developer Relations, or Product. --- Compensation ₹6–10 LPA fixed CTC 10–20% variable based on partner activation and partner-sourced pipeline. Candidates with particularly strong shipped-product experience and relevant CPaaS/AI-voice experience may be considered toward the top of the band. --- Apply If... You are someone who has built software and now wants to use that technical understanding to build partnerships, distribution, and ecosystems. If your background is purely sales/BD/partnerships without meaningful software-building experience, this role isn't the right fit. Please include your GitHub, portfolio, live product, or another concrete example of software you've built when applying.
